entries.error_pattern: Argument of type {...} is not assignable to parameter of type never (on .insert/.update)
error_symptoms: tsc/next build fails on supabase .update({...}) or .insert({...})
Type error: ... not assignable to parameter of type never
appears after adding a NEW table not in the generated Database types

solution.approach: An untyped createClient(url,key) (no <Database> generic), or a generated Database type missing the new table, infers never for insert/update payloads.
solution.answer: Type the server-only admin client as any (let _admin: any; createClient(url,key)) OR regenerate the Database types to include the new table (supabase gen types / the Management API typescript endpoint). For admin/webhook routes, any is fine.

entries.error_pattern: CREATE POLICY IF NOT EXISTS ... syntax error at or near NOT
error_symptoms: supabase db push fails on a CREATE POLICY line
auto-generated RLS migration won t apply
migration valid except the policy statements

solution.approach: Postgres has NO IF NOT EXISTS on CREATE POLICY. Guard it in a DO block checking pg_policies (idempotent + valid). CREATE TABLE/INDEX + ALTER ENABLE RLS DO support idempotent forms — only CREATE POLICY does not.
solution.answer: Replace CREATE POLICY IF NOT EXISTS "name" ON tbl ... with: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_policies WHERE schemaname=^public^ AND tablename=^tbl^ AND policyname=^name^) THEN CREATE POLICY "name" ON tbl ...; END IF; END $$;  (or DROP POLICY IF EXISTS then CREATE).

entries.error_pattern: Survey gate could never be recorded — 'survey' was in no migration, so the pipeline_gates.gate CHECK constraint rejected it; the survey result was also discarded and never rendered
error_symptoms: recordGate({gate:'survey'}) violates pipeline_gates_gate_check and throws
CHECK constraint only allowed the 8 build-stage gates (office-hours, ceo-review, eng-review, design-review, gate-1, gate-2, naive-tester, provisioned)
survey verdict shows in the panel but the per-field evidence / PRE-HARD / what-to-fix breakdown is nowhere

attempts.what: Assumed the survey gate just needed wiring in the UI
attempts.reason: the gate was structurally unrecordable — the DB CHECK constraint had no 'survey' value, and product_validation_status/pipeline_gates had no column to hold the structured result, so even a correct UI would 500 on insert

solution.approach: New idempotent migration drops and re-adds pipeline_gates_gate_check WITH 'survey' and ADDs a result JSONB column. recordGate accepts result?: unknown and inserts it; the survey route passes the full SurveyResult; the GET route selects result; ProductDetailView Step 3 renders per-field evidence (check/x + citation), PRE-HARD checks, and the toReach fix list when surveyGate.result exists.

entries.error_pattern: Card's nine validation/compliance checks lived in React state only (lost on reload) and the readiness score's compliance slice read hard_gates_passed/total columns that no migration ever created (always 0)
error_symptoms: run a test, reload, every check is back to pending
compliance portion of the readiness score is always 0
two parallel test systems: the card (ephemeral) and persisted product_validation_status columns the card never read or wrote

attempts.what: Considered repointing the card to System A (Parts A-D) persistence
attempts.reason: Parts A-D taxonomy did not match the card's 9 checks, and /validation-workflow already reads validation_test_results.qa/.naive/.gtm — i.e. it expected the breakdown keyed by the card's check ids, not Parts A-D

solution.approach: Hybrid (card checks are canonical). Migration adds hard_gates_passed/total. /validation-test rewritten to accept the nine-check payload, store the full breakdown in validation_test_results (keyed by check id), roll the 5 compliance checks into hard_gates_passed/total, and compute the composite validation_test_status (the outreach gate + the score's validation slice). The card hydrates the checks from validation_test_results on load and persists them on change via an effect, mirroring the rollup back onto product.validation so the score/gaps recompute without a refetch. Legacy Parts A-D POST path kept for safety.
solution.key_change: nine checks persist + hydrate; one rollup writer feeds score (hard_gates) + outreach gate (validation_test_status) (closes pipeline seams S6 + S7)

entries.error_pattern: run-test recomputed and wrote its OWN weighted_score_percent (passed=25/warning=20) and hard_gates_passed/total (total=9) on every test run — diverging from score.ts and colliding with the hybrid's /validation-test writer (both writing hard_gates, last-writer-wins race)
error_symptoms: weighted_score_percent disagrees with score.ts / the recalculate-score result
hard_gates_passed flips between two values depending on whether run-test or validation-test wrote last
two writers of the same columns firing within one test-run flow

attempts.what: Assumed Seam 8 was 'Step 7 calls the retired recalculate-score route'
attempts.reason: recalculate-score had already been refactored into a thin score.ts adapter (loadCardScore via readiness), so Step 7 was fine; the real divergence was run-test writing its own numbers, which also collided with the freshly-added hybrid hard_gates writer

solution.approach: Deleted run-test's entire "Recalculate weighted score after test update" block (the self-computed newScore + hardGatesPassed update). run-test now only runs a check and returns its result. Single writer each: weighted_score_percent <- score.ts via /recalculate-score (Step 7 button); hard_gates_passed/total + validation_test_status <- /validation-test (the card persist effect).
solution.key_change: removed run-test self-scoring block; score and hard_gates each have exactly one writer (closes pipeline seam S8; resolved a collision created by the S6/S7 hybrid)

entries.error_pattern: Pipeline card never reflects new survey verdicts; GET route returns a stale pipeline_gates row despite newer rows being newest in the DB
error_symptoms: card keeps showing an OLD survey verdict after running a survey or writing an override row
hard browser refresh does not fix it
cache-busting ?t= query string on the API does not fix it
runtime log shows the route's OWN query returned the stale row ('[GET] survey_gate: fail TEARDOWN 11/14') while the SAME query in the SQL editor returns the correct newest row
product_validation_status reads fresh while pipeline_gates reads stale in the same request

attempts.what: hard browser refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R)
attempts.reason: client-side; the stale data comes from the server route

attempts.what: cache-busting ?t= query string on the API URL
attempts.reason: Next data cache for the server-side fetch is not keyed on the request query string

attempts.what: Cache-Control: no-store response header (already present)
attempts.reason: governs the outgoing response only, not Next's internal server-side fetch cache

attempts.what: checked two-Supabase-project mismatch (URL + service-role key)
attempts.reason: both confirmed tfgtfhwvrswjvkyeyvsp; same DB

attempts.what: checked deployed commit is current
attempts.reason: production was 574b8fd, current

attempts.what: added export dynamic='force-dynamic' + revalidate=0 + fetchCache='force-no-store'
attempts.reason: forces every fetch in the route (incl. Supabase) to skip the data cache

solution.approach: Next.js App Router caches server-side fetches (Supabase uses fetch) by default, so the 'newest pipeline_gates row' query was served from the frozen data cache. Cache-Control:no-store on the response does NOT opt internal fetch reads out of the data cache. Force the route dynamic and disable fetch caching.
solution.key_change: Add at top, after imports: export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'; export const revalidate = 0; export const fetchCache = 'force-no-store';  RULE: every cockpit route reading live ledger/DB state that must reflect changes immediately needs these three exports. fetchCache='force-no-store' is the decisive one. This was the root cause of the recurring 'card never updates after a survey' symptom.

entries.error_pattern: Hand-merging a design-build PR via terminal hits non-fast-forward then rebase conflicts because local main drifted from remote
error_symptoms: git push rejected (non-fast-forward) after a local squash-merge
git pull --rebase conflicts on page.tsx and design-plan.md
local squash was built on an older base than current remote main

attempts.what: git merge --squash on a stale local base, then push
attempts.reason: non-fast-forward; local squash and remote main were two rebuilds from the same old base, colliding

attempts.what: git reset --hard origin/main, then git merge --squash origin/<pr-branch>
attempts.reason: PR branch was built on top of current main, so it fast-forwarded with no conflicts

solution.approach: Do not hand-resolve two near-identical rebuilds. Reset local to the true remote tip, then squash-merge the PR branch on top; commit + push (admin-bypass). The whole episode is the operator-friction anti-pattern the productised orchestrator must eliminate (merge via GitHub API on a clean base, never hand-driven).
solution.key_change: git reset --hard origin/main; git merge --squash origin/<branch>; commit; push

entries.error_pattern: Browser console shows a CSP violation blocking https://vercel.live/_next-live/feedback/feedback.js
error_symptoms: console: Loading the script 'https://vercel.live/_next-live/feedback/feedback.js' violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "script-src 'self' ...". The action has been blocked.
appears on every product built from cais-build-template-v2 and deployed to Vercel
looks like a CSP misconfiguration / defect but the app works fine

attempts.what: investigate whether the template CSP is broken / too strict
attempts.reason: the app (pages, images, fonts, Supabase) renders and works fine under the policy; only vercel.live is blocked

solution.approach: EXPECTED AND HARMLESS - not a defect. vercel.live is Vercel's own preview/feedback widget, injected by the platform, not the app. The template CSP intentionally allows script-src 'self' only, so it correctly blocks this third-party script. Only shows on Vercel deployments; real users on a custom domain never see it. Do NOT loosen the CSP to silence it. If the widget is specifically wanted on previews, add 'https://vercel.live' to script-src in that product's next.config.js - but leaving it blocked is the recommended default.
solution.key_change: No change needed. Documented as expected behaviour. CSP verified safe on deal-findrs 2026-06-03 (only vercel.live blocked; app clean).

entries.error_pattern: The naive-tester survey returns a DIFFERENT verdict on the SAME product across runs (score and PRE-HARD judgments vary run-to-run)
error_symptoms: deal-findrs run A: 13/14, P3 FAIL (two-audience landing judged incoherent)
deal-findrs run B (same site, same commit): 12/14, P3 PASS (same two-audience landing judged a coherent distributor model)
the set of 'unevidenced' fields also shifts between runs (run B flagged both Prospect type AND ICP buyer title; run A flagged Prospect type only)
verdict can flip RENOVATION/TEARDOWN-adjacent on borderline products purely from run variance

CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-06-03: same deal-findrs site/commit scored 13/14, then 12/14 RENOVATION, then 10/14 TEARDOWN across three consecutive runs — verdict flipped RENOVATION->TEARDOWN, locking downstream.

DECISIVE 2026-06-03: THREE runs on essentially-equivalent content scored 12/14 RENOVATION, 10/14 TEARDOWN, then 9/14 TEARDOWN (P2+P3 FAIL) — verdict moved the WRONG way as the site improved. The 9/14 run is SELF-CONTRADICTORY: it evidenced icp_buyer_title as 'Agency Owner / Principal' yet failed PRE-HARD P2 claiming 'no named distributor archetype' — the same run both found and denied the archetype. Conclusion: the gate is too non-deterministic to FUNCTION as a gate. Variance reduction is GATE-BREAKING priority.

attempts.what: treated the earlier P3 fail as a fixed mis-rule ('P3 miscalibrated for distributor model')
attempts.reason: it is not a deterministic wrong rule — a later run passed P3 on the identical product. The real issue is VARIANCE: the survey was an LLM judgment that landed differently across runs.

attempts.what: REMOVED the model from the survey entirely (2026-06-03)
attempts.reason: Reframed per 'generator owns invariants': the build PLANTS machine-checkable data-* markers from the card (markerProps, throws on generic/off-enum at build time); the survey GREPS them and DERIVES the verdict (P2/P3 derived from the field results, never re-judged). No model in the path. PROVEN: 3 identical runs -> TEARDOWN/TEARDOWN/TEARDOWN.

solution.approach: The survey is now a deterministic DOM-marker grep with no LLM. Build plants markers via markerProps (cais-build-template-v2/lib/surveyMarkers.ts) from the card; survey route fetches survey-manifest.json -> fetches each route's DOM -> deriveSurveyFromDom (survey-markers.ts) -> loadCardSurvey -> survey.ts. P2/P3 derived from field results (P2 IS the distributor field check) so they cannot self-contradict. Coherence enforced upstream by the build throw, not by a survey judgment. The OpenCode survey workflow (survey.yml) + SURVEY_MODE.md retired; the cockpit kickoff proxies to the deterministic route.
solution.key_change: RESOLVED 2026-06-03. Deterministic marker grep replaces LLM survey. Same input -> same verdict (proven 3x TEARDOWN). RENOVATION-determinism pending one design-build run that replants markers with named values.

entries.error_pattern: Deterministic survey scores TEARDOWN on a NAMED field whose page copy clearly states a named archetype; the planted data-* marker carries a generic category word and is banlisted
error_symptoms: survey TEARDOWN with icp_partner_type (or distributor) un-evidenced though the copy says 'buyers agent firm'
data-icp-partner-type="reseller" gets banlisted (reseller is a generic category, not an archetype)
the OLD LLM survey passed the same product; the deterministic marker grep fails it
card field value and page copy disagree (card='reseller', copy='buyers agent firm')

attempts.what: assumed it was a build/page bug and looked at page.tsx
attempts.reason: the build plants the marker from the CARD FIELD (_spec.json), not from the page copy. The card's icp_partner_type literally held 'reseller'. The deterministic survey correctly surfaces the card-copy drift the old LLM survey masked by reading the nicer copy.

solution.approach: Fix the CARD field, not the page. NAMED fields (icp_partner_type, icp_buyer_title, icp_verticals, distributor, end_user) must hold the named archetype, never the category word. Treat a banlist TEARDOWN as a card-data bug first, not a build bug. PATCH the validation route to set the archetype.
solution.code_path: PATCH /api/admin/pipeline/<slug>/validation (icp_partner_type 'reseller' -> 'buyers agent firm'); banlist in src/lib/methodology/survey-markers.ts + templates/cais-build-template-v2/lib/surveyMarkers.ts
solution.key_change: card NAMED fields carry the archetype; before dispatching design-build, check card NAMED values against the banlist (smbs, reseller, businesses, users, ...) since markerProps THROWS at build on a banlisted value

error_symptoms: next build fails with a thrown Error from markerProps naming the field + allowed set

attempts.what: treated the build failure as a code/template bug
attempts.reason: markerProps validates ENUM fields (icp_stage in seed|growth|scale|operating-business|enterprise) and NAMED fields (banlist) and THROWS by design, so an incoherent build cannot ship. The fault was the card value, not the code.

solution.approach: Set the card value so it slugifies on-set / un-banlisted. icp_stage: 'operating business' (singular) -> 'operating-business'. The throw is correct behaviour (coherence enforced at build time), not a defect.
solution.key_change: validate card ENUM/NAMED values against surveyMarkers.ts before dispatch; the build error message names the offending field + the allowed set

entries.error_pattern: Deterministic survey misses markers on non-home routes (e.g. /partners) because no survey-manifest.json exists, so it fetches '/' only
error_symptoms: distributor / end_user fields un-evidenced though their markers are planted on /partners
survey only ever grepped the homepage DOM
(historical) the old harness hardcoded ['', '/reports', '/pricing'] — missed /partners, fetched a dead /pricing anchor

attempts.what: expected the survey to discover all marker-bearing routes itself
attempts.reason: the survey route fetches public/survey-manifest.json first to learn the routes; with no manifest it falls back to ['/'] only, so markers on other routes are never seen

solution.approach: The build MUST emit public/survey-manifest.json via surveyManifest([...]) listing every marker-bearing route. The survey fetches the manifest, then greps the union of those routes' DOM.

entries.error_pattern: email rate limit hit despite custom SMTP (Resend) configured
error_symptoms: magic-link / signup emails throttled after ~2/hour
"email rate limit exceeded" on auth
SMTP set up but still limited

attempts.tried: assumed Resend or built-in email was the limiter
attempts.failed_because: Resend SMTP was correctly configured + enabled (smtp.resend.com:465, verified subdomain sender); the cap was Supabase-side, not Resend

entries.solution: Supabase Auth has its OWN hourly cap rate_limit_email_sent (default 2) that is SEPARATE from SMTP config. Switching to custom SMTP does NOT raise it. Fix: PATCH https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/{ref}/config/auth {rate_limit_email_sent: 30} via the management token (~/.supabase-token). Also note smtp_max_frequency (default 60s) throttles per-address repeats. Cockpit ref tfgtfhwvrswjvkyeyvsp raised 2->30 on 2026-06-07.

entries.product: pipeline (factory outreach engine — affects every product run through it)
entries.error_pattern: AI-composed cold-outreach openers describe the product as a DIFFERENT fabricated thing per prospect
error_symptoms: one product pitched as a dozen contradictory things (speech analytics / WCAG auditor / phone agent / nutrition planning …)
the description is riffed off the prospect’s signal, not the real product
the SAME prospect gets different product descriptions across channels

attempts.tried: tighten the compose prompt wording (“don’t embellish”)
attempts.failed_because: the real cause was an EMPTY one-liner — with nothing to ground on, prompt wording can’t stop the model inventing from the signal

entries.solution: Two parts. (1) GROUNDING SOURCE: the generate routes read product content from the WRONG table — methodology_hypothesis_cards has only mvp_url + gate state, NOT core_mechanism/promise (those live in product_validation_status), so productOneLiner came through empty. Source the one-liner from product_validation_status. (2) HARD GUARD in the composer: if the one-liner is empty, return a deterministic fallback that NAMES the product but makes NO capability claim — never call the LLM with nothing to describe; and the prompt forbids inventing/tailoring the product (it is identical for everyone; the signal personalises only the opening hook). GENERAL LESSON (portfolio-wide): an LLM given a personalisation signal but NO product grounding will fabricate a product to fit the signal — always ground product claims on a verified source and hard-fallback when absent (degrade-don’t-fake). pipeline commit 101b928.

entries.product: shared / any Next.js + @supabase/ssr middleware (the pattern ported from Corporate-AI-Solutions)
entries.error_pattern: Authenticated user is bounced to login when REFRESHING an authed page — session lost on refresh, intermittent (hits when the access token needs re-issuing)
error_symptoms: Refreshing an authed page redirects to /login (or /admin/login) despite being signed in
Session "randomly" drops after some idle time + a refresh; fine right after login
@supabase/ssr middleware using the per-cookie get/set/remove callbacks (not getAll/setAll)
Cookies sb-<ref>-auth-token.0/.1 present but partial/corrupt after a refresh

solution.approach: The middleware cookie set()/remove() callbacks reassign `response = NextResponse.next(...)` on EVERY call, discarding cookies set by prior calls. Supabase chunks the auth token across multiple cookies (…-auth-token.0/.1 + refresh); on a token refresh getUser() writes several cookies but only the LAST survives on the response → the browser gets a partial/corrupt session cookie → the next server render getUser() fails → redirect to login.
solution.answer: Create `response` ONCE; in set()/remove() write to that SAME response (response.cookies.set / request.cookies.set) and do NOT recreate it. On @supabase/ssr >=0.5 prefer the getAll/setAll pattern (writes all cookies on one response). Detection: grep middleware.ts for `response = NextResponse.next` appearing inside the cookie set/remove callbacks (count 2-3 with the get/set/remove pattern).

entries.fixed_by: pipeline middleware fix (commit 88e6948); portfolio sweep pending

entries.product: f2k-checkpoint (any repo invoking a Supabase edge function not deployed to its project)
entries.error_pattern: POST .../functions/v1/<name> returns 500 on an action, but the action still succeeds (error swallowed) — a fire-and-forget supabase.functions.invoke() to an edge function that does not exist in the repo/project.
error_symptoms: Network tab shows POST /functions/v1/send-project-creation-emails -> 500 on project create
Project is created fine anyway (call was .catch(()=>{}))
No edge function dir under supabase/functions/<name>/

attempts.tried: Assumed the edge function existed and was erroring internally
attempts.failed_because: There was no such function in the repo or on the Supabase project — the invoke 404/500s at the gateway

entries.solution: Route the notification through the repo canonical email path (src/lib/services/emailService.ts sendEmail + a template) instead of a missing edge function. F2K: createProject (src/lib/actions/projects.ts) now sends a Factory2Key transactional projectCreatedEmail to the operator, non-blocking. General rule: never leave a supabase.functions.invoke() pointing at a function that is not deployed; use the canonical service or delete the call.

entries.error_pattern: Supabase password grant returns 'Database error querying schema' after creating a user via direct SQL INSERT into auth.users
error_symptoms: POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password returns {error:'Database error querying schema'} (or 500)
the auth.users row exists, is email-confirmed, and has an encrypted_password, yet login still fails
a pre-existing user that was only UPDATEd for its password logs in fine — only freshly SQL-inserted users break
happens when provisioning QA/test accounts via the Management API SQL query endpoint (no service-role key handy)

attempts.tried: Assumed the password hash or email_confirmed_at was wrong
attempts.result: wrong — both were correct; the pre-existing user with the same setup logged in fine

attempts.tried: Compared a working (pre-existing) user vs the broken (SQL-inserted) one
attempts.result: the inserted user had NULL in GoTrue string/token columns that GoTrue expects to be empty string

solution.approach: GoTrue's login query chokes on NULL in several auth.users string columns; a bare INSERT leaves them NULL. Set them to '' (and add a matching auth.identities row for provider=email).
solution.answer: UPDATE auth.users SET confirmation_token=COALESCE(confirmation_token,''), recovery_token=COALESCE(recovery_token,''), email_change_token_new=COALESCE(email_change_token_new,''), email_change=COALESCE(email_change,''), email_change_token_current=COALESCE(email_change_token_current,''), phone_change=COALESCE(phone_change,''), phone_change_token=COALESCE(phone_change_token,''), reauthentication_token=COALESCE(reauthentication_token,'') WHERE email=...;  plus INSERT INTO auth.identities(id,user_id,identity_data,provider,provider_id,...) VALUES(gen_random_uuid(),uid,jsonb_build_object('sub',uid::text,'email',e,'email_verified',true),'email',uid::text,...). BETTER: use the GoTrue admin API POST {url}/auth/v1/admin/users with the service-role key + email_confirm:true — it sets these correctly and avoids the class.

entries.product: prelabzai (RaiseReady) — any repo pinning a DATED Anthropic model id
entries.error_pattern: AI feature silently returns no results / 500; Anthropic 404 not_found_error from a RETIRED dated model id (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-20250514)
error_symptoms: deck analysis / coaching returns nothing; deck row left stuck at status 'processing'
Anthropic API returns 404 not_found_error (NotFoundError) at request time
worked fine for weeks then broke on a specific date with NO code change
the model id is a dated snapshot like claude-sonnet-4-YYYYMMDD rather than an alias

attempts.tried: Suspected missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / env, and max_tokens truncation of the large JSON
attempts.result: Not the cause — key present; root cause was the retired dated model id

solution.approach: Anthropic retires DATED model snapshots on a published schedule (claude-sonnet-4-20250514 retired 2026-06-15). After retirement every call 404s and any try/catch surfaces it as a generic failure, so features go silent. Fix: swap to an ACTIVE model id — prefer unversioned aliases (claude-sonnet-4-5) or current-gen. CAVEAT: Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.7+ REJECT non-default temperature/top_p/top_k and budget_tokens with a 400, so a code base that passes temperature:0 needs those stripped; claude-sonnet-4-5 still accepts them and is a true drop-in.
solution.answer: Replaced claude-sonnet-4-20250514 with claude-sonnet-4-5 across the repo (drop-in: keeps temperature settings, same $3/$15 pricing). Also hardened the analyze route to mark the deck failed on any error instead of leaving it stuck at processing.
solution.code_path: lib/ai/anthropic.ts DEFAULT_MODEL + ~13 call sites (scoring/extraction/research libs, coaching/investor/founder-discovery routes, proxy pricing map)

entries.error_pattern: Next build ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND 'Cannot find module .../@caistech/report-generator/dist/render' imported from dist/index.js; fails at 'Collecting page data' AFTER 'Compiled successfully'
error_symptoms: webpack '✓ Compiled successfully' then the Vercel build ERRORs at page-data collection for the route that imports report-generator
ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for an extensionless relative import (export ... from './render') inside the package's own dist
only triggers when the package is placed in next.config serverComponentsExternalPackages

attempts.tried: Added @caistech/report-generator to serverComponentsExternalPackages alongside @react-pdf/renderer (to keep native deps out of the bundle)
attempts.result: Made it WORSE — Node's native ESM loader then resolves the package and rejects the extensionless './render' import (ESM fullySpecified)

solution.approach: report-generator ships ESM ("type":"module") with extensionless relative imports, which neither Node's native ESM loader (when externalized) nor webpack's fullySpecified ESM resolver accept. Do NOT externalize it; transpilePackages it so Next/SWC bundles it and relaxes fullySpecified. Keep @react-pdf/renderer externalized (native fontkit deps) — it stays external transitively even though its importer is bundled.
solution.answer: next.config.js: transpilePackages: ['@caistech/report-generator']; serverComponentsExternalPackages keeps '@react-pdf/renderer' (NOT report-generator). Route runtime='nodejs'. Smoke test: an unauthenticated POST returns 401 (not 500) => the module + react-pdf loaded at runtime.

entries.product: @caistech/report-generator (all branded-PDF consumers) — found via prelabzai readiness report
entries.error_pattern: Branded PDF shows literal HTML entities (' for apostrophe, & for &), drops/mis-renders non-Latin1 glyphs (arrow -> shows as stray quote/blank), and orphans list bullets (lone bullet at page bottom, its text on the next page)
error_symptoms: every apostrophe/quote in the PDF body renders as the literal string '
ampersands render as &
unicode arrows (U+2192) render as a stray quote or blank — em-dash and bullet render fine (they are WinAnsi)
a bullet appears at the bottom of a page with its text pushed to the top of the next page

attempts.tried: Assumed the analysis TEXT stored in the DB was HTML-escaped
attempts.result: No — the DB holds clean text and the on-screen (browser) rendering is fine; the escaping is introduced by the PDF renderer

solution.approach: The package's Markdown component fed marked.lexer's token.text (which marked HTML-ESCAPES: ' -> ', & -> &) straight into react-pdf <Text>, which renders the literal string (react-pdf does NOT decode HTML entities). react-pdf's built-in Helvetica is WinAnsi-only so glyphs like the arrow drop. And list items were plain Views that split across page breaks. Fix is IN THE PACKAGE (v0.1.1): cleanText() decodes marked's named+numeric entities and swaps out-of-WinAnsi glyphs (arrows/smart-quotes/ellipsis) to ASCII (leave dashes + bullet), applied at every leaf text node; wrap={false} on the list-item View.
solution.answer: Published @caistech/report-generator@0.1.1 (cleanText + wrap=false); consumers bump to >=0.1.1. Verified against the exact failing strings.

entries.product: Kira (4 rounds) + @caistech/elevenlabs-convai — pattern applies to EVERY convai memory consumer
entries.error_pattern: Voice agent does not remember a prior conversation. User briefs the agent at length, reconnects, and it has no recall ("I don't have access to past conversations" / greets on a stale objective). Memory was "fixed" 4+ separate times over 6 months and stayed broken each time.
error_symptoms: agent greets with a stale/first-ever objective instead of recent context
agent says it cannot access past conversations despite a wired memory loop
kira_memory / memory table is empty or only holds seed rows
no error anywhere — tool webhooks 200 or are simply never called; the failure is SILENT in every layer
each fix round's commit message independently asserts "memory never actually worked"

attempts.tried: Bind the post-call webhook (2026-05-25) — per-agent platform_settings.webhook → workspace-scoped bindWorkspaceWebhook
attempts.result: Correct fix for link 1. Memory still broken — link 4 was also broken.

attempts.tried: Remove hardcoded webhook-secret fallback + adopt hub HMAC verifier (2026-05-25)
attempts.result: Correct fix for link 2. Memory still broken.

attempts.tried: Correct tool-router auth to header-secret, not post-call HMAC (2026-05-25)
attempts.result: Correct fix for link 4. Memory still broken — link 7 was broken.

attempts.tried: Adopt the canonical @caistech/elevenlabs-convai loop wholesale (2026-07-20)
attempts.result: Correct architecture. Memory still broken — links 6 and 7 broken.

attempts.tried: Fix get_conversation_context status filter — "welcome-back recall never fired" (2026-07-20)
attempts.result: Correct fix for link 7. Memory still broken — link 6 (distil) was broken.

attempts.tried: Wire post-call distillation — "kira_memory was never filling" (2026-07-20)
attempts.result: Correct fix for link 6. Memory still broken — link 5 (agent never CALLS the tool) was broken.

attempts.tried: Create the kira_logs table its writers assumed (2026-07-20)
attempts.result: Removed a silent-fail residual that had been HIDING the breaks above.

solution.approach: The loop is a CHAIN of 7 independent links, and a break in ANY one produces the identical, silent "agent has no memory" symptom: (1) post-call webhook bound at workspace scope; (2) post-call HMAC verifies; (3) memory tools ATTACHED to the agent (tool_ids); (4) tool-webhook auth header matches (re-provision required whenever the secret changes); (5) the agent MODEL actually emits the tool call; (6) post-call distil writes durable memory rows; (7) recall reads them back with the right filters. Every round above correctly fixed one link while another was still broken, so each fix was real AND the system stayed broken. The root cause of the RECURRENCE is not any single link — it is that no test ever exercised the whole chain (talk → disconnect → reconnect → assert recall), so "fixed" was always inferred from code, never observed from behaviour.
solution.answer: Do not debug links individually. Add ONE end-to-end behavioural test as the definition of done: hold a real conversation, disconnect, reconnect, assert the agent names a specific fact from the prior call. Run it in CI against prod. Any of the 4 rounds above would have failed it on day one. Treat a green unit/route test as evidence of NOTHING for this subsystem.
solution.code_path: kira: lib/kira/convai.ts (loop mount), app/api/kira/create/route.ts (provisioning), app/api/kira/webhooks/* (7 routes), scripts/reprovision-kira-agents.mjs. hub: @caistech/elevenlabs-convai createConvaiWebhookRoutes / createConversationTools / distillConversationToMemory.

entries.product: Kira — applies to any repo that hardcodes the agent LLM instead of taking DEFAULT_AGENT_LLM
entries.error_pattern: Voice agent with a correctly-wired memory loop still never remembers, because the agent MODEL silently stops emitting tool calls. Every route, table, secret and webhook is correct; the tools are simply never invoked.
error_symptoms: memory tables stay empty but no route ever 4xx/5xx — because no request arrives
recall works in a short test call and degrades as the conversation lengthens
agent verbally claims it cannot access memory/documents rather than erroring
the repo pins a recent @caistech/elevenlabs-convai yet passes its own `llm:` value

attempts.tried: Audited webhook binding, HMAC, tool attachment, tool auth header, table columns, RLS
attempts.result: All correct — the wiring was not the fault.

solution.approach: @caistech/elevenlabs-convai sets DEFAULT_AGENT_LLM = gpt-4.1-mini (v0.4.2, commit c408d98) SPECIFICALLY because gpt-4o-mini drops tool calls over long conversations. Kira provisions agents through a raw ElevenLabs POST that hardcodes `llm: gpt-4o-mini`, bypassing the hub default entirely — so the one repo that mounted the full loop correctly overrode the one setting that makes it fire. Memory that is never CALLED is indistinguishable from memory that does not exist.
solution.answer: Never hardcode the agent LLM. Take DEFAULT_AGENT_LLM from the hub package, or route provisioning through the hub createAgent(). When auditing a "memory does not work" report, check the MODEL before the plumbing — it is the cheapest check and it produces zero error signal.

entries.product: portfolio-wide — @caistech/elevenlabs-convai (audit 2026-07-25), pattern applies to any shared-service rollout claim
entries.error_pattern: A shared capability is reported as "rolled out to every repo" when only the PACKAGE was installed. Consuming repos get the widget and none of the behaviour, so the capability is believed live portfolio-wide while working in exactly one repo.
error_symptoms: package.json shows the dependency in N repos — used as the rollout evidence
the behaviour fails in a repo everyone believed was covered
no repo-level check distinguishes "imports the package" from "mounts its routes"
version drift across consumers goes unnoticed (0.1.6 → 0.5.0 in the same portfolio)

attempts.tried: Grepping package.json for the dependency across repos to confirm rollout
attempts.result: FALSE POSITIVE — proves installation, not integration. This is the check that produced the overclaim.

solution.approach: Measured 2026-07-25 across 20 repos depending on @caistech/elevenlabs-convai: exactly ONE (Kira) mounts all three legs (start_conversation + recall_memory + distil). Mova + PrelabzAI mount recall/start but no distil (storage, not memory). Corporate-AI-Solutions + LingoPureAI + pipeline distil but expose no recall route (writes nobody reads). The remaining 14 mount none of it — widget only. Version spread 0.1.6 (MMCBuild) → 0.5.0 (Kira).
solution.answer: Verify rollout by ROUTE PRESENCE, never by dependency presence. The mechanical check: for each consumer assert the existence of the recall route dir, the start_conversation route dir, and a distillConversationToMemory reference. Add it to feature-preflight / check-shared-forks so an unmounted consumer fails CI instead of being counted as covered. Record per-consumer mount status in SHARED_SERVICES.md so the next session cannot re-infer coverage from package.json.
solution.code_path: audit: find <repo> -type d -name recall_memory / -name start_conversation; grep -rl distillConversationToMemory. Guard belongs in cais-shared-services/scripts/.

entries.product: Kira — class applies to every prompted agent across the portfolio
entries.error_pattern: The system prompt lists tools the agent does not have. The agent, behaving correctly, tells the user it "cannot access" the capability — which reads to the user as a broken product rather than an unbuilt one. The upstream half of the feature (ingestion/UI) ships and the retrieval half never does.
error_symptoms: agent says "I can't access that document" / "I can't access URLs" for a documented feature
an upload UI and ingest route exist and write rows successfully
no retrieval route exists for the agent to call — the store is write-only
the prompt enumerates the tool by name, so the agent believes it should work

attempts.tried: Attaching the named tools to close the gap
attempts.result: Correct instinct, but attaching a tool whose route does not exist makes the agent call a 404 — a worse failure. The route must be built first.

solution.approach: Kira built the whole ingestion half on 2026-01-19..21 — kira_knowledge table, /api/kira/knowledge/upload, /api/kira/knowledge/url, embeddings, Jina reranking, hybrid semantic search in lib/kira/knowledge-search.ts. The retrieval webhook route the voice agent would call was never created. lib/kira/convai.ts:113-115 documents this honestly ("their routes do not exist yet"), while lib/kira/prompts.ts:404-417 has advertised search_knowledge / search_web / start_research_session / save_finding to the agent for six months. Unlike the memory loop this was never re-built — it was built halfway ONCE and asserted complete ever since, which feels identical from the user's seat.
solution.answer: The prompt's tool list must be GENERATED from the attached tool set, never hand-written — a hand-written list drifts into a lie the moment attachment changes. Until then, add a provisioning-time assertion that every tool named in the prompt exists in the agent's tool_ids and every attached tool resolves to a live route. A capability the agent claims and lacks is a product defect, not a prompt nit.
solution.code_path: kira: lib/kira/prompts.ts:404-417 (the claim), lib/kira/convai.ts:113-115 (the honest comment), lib/kira/knowledge-search.ts (built, unreachable), app/api/kira/knowledge/* (ingest half only).

entries.product: Kira — class applies to any repo with more than one way to create the same resource
entries.error_pattern: A second, older code path that provisions the same resource (agent/account/tenant) is left in place when the canonical path is modernised. It stops being exercised, so it silently rots — and then fires on a rare trigger (first real payment, first invite, first import) and mints a broken resource nobody is looking for.
error_symptoms: two functions with the same job in different files, one obviously older
the stale path is never hit in testing because its trigger is rare (a real paid checkout)
the stale copy accumulates every fix the canonical path received and it did not: no tools attached, no model pinned, deprecated API shapes, hardcoded secret fallbacks
DB rows created by the two paths differ in shape (one sets agent_name, the other sets name)

attempts.tried: Patching the stale path to match the canonical one
attempts.result: Rejected — it just recreates the divergence with a fresh timestamp. Two paths means the next fix lands in one of them again.

solution.approach: Kira's Stripe webhook carried its own createElevenLabsAgent() frozen at Jan-2026: no memory tools attached (zero memory loop), no llm pinned, the deprecated platform_settings.webhook shape ElevenLabs silently ignores, a hardcoded `|| 'kira-webhook-secret'` fallback, no origin allowlist, a 4th copy of the system prompt, and it wrote kira_agents.name where canonical writes agent_name. It ALSO inserted a bare public.users row with no auth_user_id — an orphan account with no possible login. Proof it had never fired: every agent row in prod carries a draft_id, i.e. all came from /api/kira/create. It was a landmine awaiting the first real paid checkout.
solution.answer: DELETE the duplicate rather than repair it — there must be exactly one provisioning path. Here the webhook had no business minting agents at all: accounts belong to /api/onboarding/complete (which creates a real confirmed auth.users and lets the trigger link the app row) and agents belong to /api/kira/create (the only path that attaches tools + continuity prompt + allowlist + post-call webhook). A payment webhook records SUBSCRIPTION STATE and nothing else. Also handle the race: the webhook often arrives before the buyer sets their password, so it must no-op when the account is absent, never create one.
solution.code_path: kira: app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts (removed handleCheckoutComplete provisioning + createElevenLabsAgent + generateKiraPrompt + sendWelcomeEmail), canonical paths app/api/kira/create/route.ts + app/api/onboarding/complete/route.ts

entries.product: Kira (email sender) — class applies portfolio-wide to every `process.env.X || <literal>` default
entries.error_pattern: A scaffold placeholder left as the `||` fallback of an env var becomes the LIVE production value because the env var was never actually set anywhere. Nothing errors at boot; the feature just silently fails at the far end (rejected email, wrong host, wrong sender).
error_symptoms: transactional email 'sends' with no thrown error but never arrives
a literal placeholder domain/host (yourdomain.com, example.com, localhost:3000) in a `||` default
the env var is documented in README/.env.example but present in no real environment
the failure is invisible because the send path try/catches and logs

attempts.tried: Checking the Resend API key and dashboard
attempts.result: Key was valid — the FROM address was the fault, not auth.

solution.approach: lib/email/resend.ts had `const FROM_EMAIL = process.env.EMAIL_FROM || 'Kira <kira@yourdomain.com>'`. EMAIL_FROM was set in no environment, so every transactional email Kira ever sent was addressed from an unverified placeholder domain and rejected by Resend. The removed Stripe welcome email carried the same literal inline.
solution.answer: A `||` fallback must be the correct PRODUCTION value, never a placeholder — if there is no safe default, throw at startup instead. Portfolio rule: the only Resend-verified sending subdomain is updates.corporateaisolutions.com (the bare apex is NOT verified), so that is the default. Grep any repo for placeholder literals (yourdomain.com / example.com / localhost) sitting in `||` defaults; each one is a silently-live production value.

entries.product: @caistech/elevenlabs-convai consumers — verified exposed: singify-platform; gated: prelabzai, sayfix; fixed: kira
entries.error_pattern: Voice-agent memory tool routes (recall_memory/save_memory/start_conversation) accept unauthenticated POSTs. Where start_conversation is NOT session-gated, a public agent id (readable from the client bundle) mints a conversation bound to the agent owner, and recall then returns that owner's memory — a cross-tenant read/write.
error_symptoms: tool webhook request_headers is Content-Type only — no shared-secret or HMAC
start_conversation returns 200 "Agent not found" for a synthetic agent id (no session gate) instead of 401
recall_memory / save_memory return 200 and derive identity from conversation_id with no auth
the agent id is NEXT_PUBLIC / present in the client bundle

attempts.tried: Probing with synthetic agent/conversation ids to read the auth model without exfiltrating any real memory
attempts.result: Established: singify start has no session gate (exposed); prelabz + sayfix return 401 Unauthorized session (gated at the door); all three leave recall/save unauthenticated

solution.approach: Two-tier reality: repos that session-gate start_conversation (prelabz, sayfix) are protected because the identity-binding conversation row can only be created by a verified session; a repo that does NOT session-gate it (singify) is exposed via the public agent id — the same hole Kira had. Kira patched it with a shared-secret header (x-kira-tool-secret) on the tool webhooks plus a toolSecretOk() route guard, but that is a per-repo workaround because createConversationTools hardcodes Content-Type and offers no auth hook.
solution.answer: Durable fix belongs in @caistech/elevenlabs-convai: createConversationTools must accept a shared secret and the route handlers must fail-closed without it (HANDOFF_RESPONSE P1). Until then, patch each exposed repo workspace tools in place with the header (scripts/patch-tool-secret-headers.mjs pattern) AND ensure start_conversation is session-gated. Verify rollout by probing start_conversation with a synthetic agent id: a 200 "Agent not found" means no session gate = exposed; a 401 means gated.
solution.code_path: @caistech/elevenlabs-convai createConversationTools (no auth hook) + webhook-handlers.handleStartConversation; kira reference fix lib/kira/convai.ts toolSecretOk + scripts/patch-tool-secret-headers.mjs

entries.product: @caistech/elevenlabs-convai (createConversationTools) + every consumer — Kira, likely Singify (same pattern)
entries.error_pattern: A voice agent CALLS its memory/knowledge tools (tool_calls fire) but they always return "first chat" / "conversation not found" / empty — so memory and document retrieval never work in a REAL voice call, even though the webhooks work when called directly.
error_symptoms: agent audibly says "this is our first chat" / "I do not have that saved" despite real history
simulate-conversation shows the tool_calls firing, yet responses are empty
direct POST to the webhook with the correct conversation_id works perfectly (so the route + DB are fine)
the tool parameter conversation_id / elevenlabs_conversation_id has is_system_provided=false and dynamic_variable=""

attempts.tried: Checked model (gpt-4.1-mini), tool attachment (tool_ids present), tool-secret header, HMAC, RLS — all correct
attempts.result: None was the fault; the agent was calling the tools but they could not identify the conversation

solution.approach: The tool id parameters (conversation_id, elevenlabs_conversation_id, elevenlabs_agent_id) were LLM-FILLED — the model cannot know ElevenLabs' real conversation id, so it passed a placeholder/garbage, the webhook could not bind the conversation, and identity resolution failed. This is the true bottom of the "memory never worked" onion: link 5 (agent emits the call) actually worked; the CALL PAYLOAD was unusable. A direct-call E2E test hides it because the test supplies the id.
solution.answer: Bind the id params to ElevenLabs SYSTEM DYNAMIC VARIABLES so ElevenLabs injects the real values into the webhook body: conversation_id/elevenlabs_conversation_id -> dynamic_variable "system__conversation_id"; elevenlabs_agent_id -> "system__agent_id". These are auto-populated on ALL channels (web/WebRTC/widget included; only caller_id/called_number are voice-only). A param bound this way must set ONLY dynamic_variable among {description,dynamic_variable,is_system_provided,constant_value,is_omitted} (API 422s otherwise). Workspace tools are shared across agents and ensureWorkspaceTools never overwrites config, so patching the workspace tools once fixes all agents; the DURABLE fix is to build the tools with these bindings in createConversationTools (canonical).
solution.code_path: kira: scripts/patch-tool-system-vars.mjs (the patch); canonical fix belongs in @caistech/elevenlabs-convai createConversationTools/toWorkspaceToolConfig so fresh tools carry the bindings. Verify with the simulate-conversation API (it flags missing system dynamic variables).

entries.error_pattern: Too many requests. You can only make 10 requests per second. See rate limit response headers
entries.error_symptoms: A serial email fan-out silently loses recipients from about the 10th send onward. The operator sees a mostly-successful run; only the per-recipient receipt row shows status=failed with the rate-limit text. Nothing retries.

attempts.tried: Sent every recipient in a tight serial for-loop with no delay, on the assumption that serial implies safe
attempts.result: FAILED — a serial loop with no network wait still exceeds 10 req/sec. Recipient 11 of an 11-recipient estate announcement was dropped on the first live run.

solution.approach: Pace the loop under the provider cap: await a 150ms delay (~6.7/sec) before every send after the first. Applies to ANY bulk serial Resend loop — admin notification fan-outs, bulk agent email, multi-recipient digests — not just the one where it was found. Record a per-recipient outcome so a partial send is visible rather than assumed clean.
solution.code_path: src/lib/estates/archive-notify.ts — SEND_INTERVAL_MS + delay() at the top of the deliver() closure

entries.fixed_by: claude-code (f2k estate status announcement first live run)

entries.error_pattern: invalid input syntax for type uuid — audit_log row never written
entries.error_symptoms: An admin action returns 200 and the UI promises an audit trail, but audit_log holds zero rows for that action, ever. No error reaches the operator; the failure exists only as a server console.error.

attempts.tried: Assumed the audit write succeeded because the helper is awaited and the route returned 200
attempts.result: FAILED — the helper swallows insert errors with console.error only, so the caller cannot distinguish success from failure

attempts.tried: Queried audit_log by action name and found nothing; suspected the action string was wrong
attempts.result: FAILED — the action string was correct; the INSERT itself was being rejected

solution.approach: audit_log.entity_id is a uuid column. Passing a TEXT business key (an estate slug, a repo name) makes Postgres reject the insert on the uuid cast. Pass entity_id: null and carry the text key inside the details jsonb. Audit every auditLog call whose entity is keyed by slug or name rather than a UUID — and prefer surfacing insert failures over console.error, since a silently-missing audit trail is indistinguishable from one that was never attempted.

entries.error_pattern: Console diagnosis card announces a drafted fix plan, but there is no control to activate it or take the ticket forward
entries.error_symptoms: A ticket shows "Code fix — plan drafted" with no plan text beneath it and no Approve plan → build button anywhere. The Scope with Claude panel — the only forward path — is not rendered, and the card tells the operator to use a button "in the scope panel below" that is not on the page. The degraded diagnosis also asserts an unrelated prior fix as the root cause.

attempts.tried: Assumed the promote route was broken or blocked by write permissions
attempts.result: FAILED — /api/tickets/[id]/scope/promote works and already accepts an explicit { plan } in the request body

attempts.tried: Assumed the Investigate pass had not produced a plan message
attempts.result: PARTLY — it posts the plan as an assistant message ONLY when verdict is code_fix AND plan_markdown exists; the degraded keyword path returns code_fix with no plan, so nothing is ever posted and the button can never light up

solution.approach: Three coupled defects, all on the console ticket surface. (1) The plan drafted by Investigate lives on tickets.diagnosis.plan_markdown, but the only promote control read a "## Plan" out of an assistant message in the scope thread — a different source — so a plan could be displayed with nothing to action it. Put the button ON the plan being displayed, posting it to the existing promote route via its { plan } body. (2) The scope panel was gated to escalated/failure states or an existing thread, so an open ticket (state preparing, no messages) had no forward path at all; render it for every non-closed state. (3) The keyword fallback returned verdict code_fix with no plan_markdown while the badge hardcoded the label "Code fix — plan drafted", announcing work that was never done. The fallback must never claim code_fix (that verdict promises a promotable plan it cannot write), and a keyword KB hit is an unverified LEAD, not a root cause — asserting one produced a magic-link email failure "explained" by an unrelated note about estate registration pages (degrade-don't-fake, DATA_STANDARD R4).
solution.code_path: src/components/console/PromotePlan.tsx (new); src/lib/console/diagnosis.ts + src/lib/__tests__/console-diagnosis.test.ts (new — pins the badge honesty rule); src/app/console/[id]/page.tsx; src/app/api/tickets/[id]/investigate/route.ts

entries.error_pattern: kira_tasks.status contains a JSON object ({"taskGroupId":...,"status":"queued","draft":{...}}) instead of one of the six TaskState strings
entries.error_symptoms: Tasks are in the database and on NO page. /admin/asked-for looks calm, the approval flow finds nothing, the owner is told his email was drafted and it never sends. Rows have handled_by='orchestrator' and a non-terminal status. Nothing errors; no log line; the row looks healthy in the table. Only rows older than the 15-minute grace window are affected, which makes it look like a dispatch bug when the dispatch was fine.

attempts.tried: Inspected the dispatch-time writer (lib/kira/swarm/tool-handlers.ts mirrorTask, status: result.status) and the wire adapter (orchestrator-adapter.ts) and the orchestrator's own /v1/dispatch route
attempts.result: FAILED to explain it - all three are correct on disk. Led to a false 'the deployed build must differ from main' theory. It did not; deployed == origin/main.

attempts.tried: Compared deployed Vercel production against origin/main HEAD
attempts.result: Ruled out deploy drift - no unpushed commits, latest prod deploy is the current HEAD

attempts.tried: Grepped for EVERY writer of the table rather than the obvious two
attempts.result: SUCCESS - found a third writer nobody had checked: the reconcile cron

solution.approach: app/api/cron/reconcile-tasks/route.ts called coordinator.getTaskState(), which returns a TaskStatus OBJECT, then wrote `status: live` (the object) instead of `live.status`. The guard hid it: `live === task.status` compares an object to a string, so it is NEVER equal, every row looked changed, and every 20-minute run rewrote the same damage. Fix: read live.status, validate it with a new runtime validator asTaskState() (a bare `x as TaskState` cast validates nothing and is what let an object through), skip the row when unreadable, and add a CHECK constraint on kira_tasks.status so the write errors instead of persisting. GENERAL LESSON: when a column holds a serialised object, enumerate EVERY writer of that table - the culprit is the one nobody thought was a writer - and never trust an equality guard that compares across types.

entries.error_pattern: Supabase Auth /otp and /recover return 500 unexpected_failure "Error sending magic link email"; auth_logs show gomail: could not send email 1: 550 "The updates.corporateaisolutions.com domain is not verified. Please, add and verify your domain on https://resend.com/domains"
entries.error_symptoms: Admin cannot log in; magic link and forgot-password produce no email while password login still works; the app's OWN Resend sends (registration acknowledgements, digests) keep delivering fine; DNS for the sending subdomain (SPF, DKIM, feedback MX) is fully intact; Supabase auth config looks healthy (custom SMTP enabled, rate_limit_email_sent 30, redirect allowlist correct); no deploy failed and production is running the current commit

attempts.tried: Suspected the domain lost verification (the message says so, and a prior SayFix fix had exactly that cause) — checked SPF/DKIM/MX for updates.corporateaisolutions.com via DNS
attempts.result: WRONG PATH. All records present and correct (SPF include:amazonses.com, resend._domainkey DKIM, feedback-smtp MX in ap-northeast-1). The 550 does not mean DNS is broken.

attempts.tried: Suspected the admin allowlist or the auth_user_id link broke in the Seoul->Sydney migration — joined public.admin_users to auth.users
attempts.result: Ruled out. uwe@factory2key.com.au is super_admin, linked to a confirmed auth user with a password, last sign-in 2026-06-30.

attempts.tried: Suspected middleware / callback drift or a stale production deploy — reviewed src/middleware.ts, /api/auth/callback (PKCE) and /api/auth/confirm (token_hash), and compared the deployed commit SHA to origin/main
attempts.result: Ruled out. Minted a magiclink token_hash with admin/generate_link and walked it through /api/auth/confirm on production: 307 -> /admin, session cookie set, /admin rendered. Every code path works; only DELIVERY was broken.

attempts.tried: Read Supabase auth_logs (Management API analytics/endpoints/logs.all) for the failing request id
attempts.result: FOUND IT. The 550 came from Resend at send time, meaning the SMTP credential authenticated but its account has no verified sending domain.

attempts.tried: Compared the Vercel RESEND_API_KEY updatedAt to the last successful app email and the last successful admin login
attempts.result: CONFIRMED. RESEND_API_KEY was rotated in Vercel 2026-06-29 11:50 UTC to a key from a different Resend account (the mcmdennis org). Supabase Auth's own smtp_pass copy was never updated, so it kept the OLD account's key. All auth email dead from 2026-06-29; unnoticed for a month because password login still worked.

solution.approach: Supabase Auth stores its OWN copy of the Resend API key in smtp_pass, independent of the app's Vercel RESEND_API_KEY. Rotating the app's key does not update Supabase's, and nothing surfaces the divergence. THE DISCRIMINATOR for the identical 550/400 'domain is not verified' message: call GET https://api.resend.com/domains with THAT SPECIFIC KEY. If the domain is absent, the key is from the wrong Resend account (this bug — fix the key). If it is present but status != verified, verification genuinely lapsed (fix DNS — the earlier SayFix case). Do not start with DNS. Fix: PATCH https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/{ref}/config/auth {smtp_pass: <current key>} with the management token from ~/.supabase-token, then PROVE it by POSTing /auth/v1/otp and confirming a 200 plus a delivered status in the Resend API — a saved config is not a working send.
solution.code_path: scripts/repair-auth-smtp.mjs (f2k-projects) — reads RESEND_API_KEY from .env.local without printing it, refuses to push a key whose account lacks the verified domain, PATCHes Supabase Auth, then verifies with a real send. Diagnosis path: GET /v1/projects/{ref}/analytics/endpoints/logs.all?sql=select ... from auth_logs — the only place the underlying SMTP error is visible; the client only ever sees a generic 500.

usage: Before fixing ANY bug, grep this file for matching error patterns. Also check SayFix DB for product-specific attempts.

execute sends an HMAC webhook to INVESTORPILOT_WEBHOOK_URL with PIPELINE_INTAKE_WEBHOOK_SECRET; if either env is missing it logs "No webhook URL - skipping" and returns a dry-run would_execute (silent no-op). Set both in Vercel (Production/Preview) AND ensure a live receiver verifies the same secret. Related: cas-pipeline-execute-dry-run-default.

magic-link signs into a separate Supabase project via INVESTORPILOT_SUPABASE_URL/KEY + NEXT_PUBLIC_INVESTORPILOT_URL (the last is build-time/NEXT_PUBLIC -> needs a rebuild, not just redeploy). Set them and confirm the IP project accepts OTP with the redirect configured.
